doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Riverside and the New York scene
title: Gigs with Buddy De Franco, Cafe Bohemia, and Monk's Music
summary: Ware is working constantly, plays with Buddy De Franco, leads his own trio at the Bohemia and Birdland, and records Monk's Music with Hawkins and Coltrane.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: It was an old German flatback bass; the same bass that he used. Anyway, I started gigging at Riverside and people started calling me; my Buddy De Franco called me for a week, and I got my union card straight, my New York card straight, for that engagement down at the Cafe Bohemia -- that was a popular spot, in the Village.

Oh, from there, I started -- I was working so much, making money but I wasn't realizing any of it because I was going after that stuff, but I was recording almost every day; I had matinees to play; I mean, one week working with Buddy, the next week they wanted me to work down in Birdland, on a Sunday, and I'm rehearsing late that afternoon with Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd and, oh, I forgot the piano player's name, but they formed a group; they made an album that I was supposed to make ... I was so tired I couldn't make the date, like on a Monday, I couldn't make it -- I finished that week down there at the Bohemia.
And the club owner, he liked me; I don't know, something about me he liked, maybe because I was easy going, I'd smile, you know, or something.
Oh is that so? Well, anyway, I had a little gig, I had my own trio at the Bohemia, and even Birdland, one of the owners ... I forgot the name; the fellow that

got killed; he liked me, and he'd have me down there on Monday night, you know, with my own group, and I tried to get reliable guys to make it, and I was doing very well, you know, and everybody I ran into, there'd be somebody wanting me to work with them.
And this was all in the arly fifties, I mean, middle fifties, '57 --
This was before the monk and train period?
I was just getting in to the monk and train period. See, because we got ready to do Thelonious (unintelligible) that's the one with Coleman Hawkins and ...
Riverside, yes, uh huh. We did that, and then we did this -- now, we did that month with Ray Copelan, GG and Art Blakie, and Coleman Hawkins and myself.
Monk's Music Gigi, Blakey, I said Coltrane
